title: Adaptive micro-batch shaping for dynamic sequence-length bucketing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large variance in client request sequence lengths causes excessive padding across micro-batches, increasing GPU compute and memory usage. Existing scheduler batches by arrival time and simple size thresholds; this leads to up to 40% wasted tokens on some workloads (short-chat heavy) and unpredictable tail latencies when a long prefill arrives into an otherwise short batch.

Goal: Implement an adaptive micro-batch shaping system that dynamically buckets requests by prefill sequence-length distribution and applies per-worker padding policies to minimize padded tokens while preserving latency SLOs and KV-cache reuse patterns. Target metrics: reduce padded-token overhead by >=30% on mixed workloads, improve throughput per-GPU by 15-25% for chat-heavy traffic, maintain 95th percentile decode latency within +5% of baseline.

Scope: Scheduler + runtime kernel selection hooks + KV cache alignment. Implementation must work with hosted and Dedicated modes and be configurable via runtime flags and Console tuning UI.

Constraints: Changes must not invalidate KV cache for other concurrent streams more than necessary; memory fragmentation on GPUs must be bounded; fallbacks required if dynamic bucketing underperforms (revert to legacy batching policy).
acceptance_criteria: New bucketing scheduler reduces padded-token overhead by >=30% on 3 benchmark workloads (chat-short, mix-chat-long, embeddings-mixed)
End-to-end throughput improvement of 15-25% on Dedicated benchmark harness with p95 decode latency <= baseline * 1.05
Feature toggle exists (runtime flag + console control) to enable/disable micro-batch shaping per deployment
Automated regression tests for KV-cache alignment and padding correctness
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed and signed-off by infra, runtime, and PM
implementation_plan: Instrument prefill histogram per-route (hist bins 0-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,257-512,>512) - data collection phase (A)
Prototype bucketing policy in scheduler: greedy first-fit into micro-batches with max-token budget; evaluate on offline replay (B)
Add runtime kernel selection hints: pass bucket metadata so kernel can choose packing strategy (C)
KV-cache alignment: implement soft-join policy where compatible KV caches are reused only when bucketed sequence length delta < 8 tokens (D)
Implement monitoring: padded-token ratio, per-bucket p95/p99 latencies, memory headroom metrics (E)
Canary rollout: 5% traffic in staging, then 20% in dedicated clusters, monitor regressions, then full rollout (F)
decisions: Use histogram-driven bucketing (online adaptive) instead of per-request clustering to keep compute overhead low
Choose greedy first-fit packing with periodic re-evaluation over optimal bin-packing (NP-hard) because it hits 90-95% of optimum with far less scheduling cost
Prefer soft KV-cache reuse (delta threshold) instead of strict invalidation to avoid excessive cache misses on small length differences
Expose a per-deployment padding_budget_pct parameter in Console to allow ops teams to dial trade-offs
tradeoffs: + Reduced padded tokens and GPU compute cost; improved throughput for short-heavy workloads
- Added scheduler complexity and slightly higher CPU scheduling overhead (target <3% CPU bound increase)
- Potential for higher tail latency in pathological interleaving cases; mitigated via soft thresholds and fallback policies
- KV-cache fragmentation risk when matching by bucket; limited by choosing conservative delta thresholds
benchmark_results: Local replay (mix-chat-long): baseline padded-token ratio 0.38 -> prototype 0.24 (-36%)
Dedicated harness (p3.8x): baseline throughput 12.5 reqs/s -> shaped micro-batches 15.2 reqs/s (+21%), p95 decode latency +3%
Edge-case long-prefill test: small regression in p99 for mixed bursts; mitigations reduced p99 gap from +22% to +6%
